text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers add new code to a shared project, automated builds start immediately. These builds check that the code works correctly and produce a new version of the software. At the same time, the system runs tests to make sure nothing has broken. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. CI pipelines organise all these steps into a clear process, so every change is checked in the same way. As a result, teams can work faster and with more confidence.
